Thanks, Stephanie. Quick checklist/questions from product/security perspective:

1) Canary approach — I'd propose a staged canary (1% -> 10% -> 50%) but with the no-fallback constraint that means we need to be able to traffic-shift back to zero immediately if we see any data-quality or availability issues.
2) Observability — required: per-request provenance (model id, node id, region), token-level cost breakdown, and realtime error-rate dashboards.
3) Auditability — enable long retention audit logs for the pilot (we'll need an S3 path + access controls).
4) SLA/compensations — CareBridge should acknowledge that no-fallback increases risk; discuss credits if we miss latency or availability targets.
5) Cost — enforcing redwood-secure-1b-quant (no fallback to smaller models) will increase per-token cost; include an estimate in the MOP.

Recommendation: approve a timeboxed pilot (6 weeks) with a gating checklist before full production. Condition approval on: signed waiver (they sign the operational risk waiver), an approved rollback/abort plan, and a pre-flight load test.

I'll sketch the pilot_config.yaml and a short waiver doc; can someone add the SLA/commercial language?

Technical notes / feasibility:

- Enforced model selection: we can pin a request route to redwood-secure-1b-quant using route-level immutable_model_id in the control plane. That will prevent automated variant substitution.
- Region lock: routing policy can be constrained to us-east-1 and we'll configure the smart-router to reject any cross-region hop.
- No-fallback behavior: default runtime retries and fallback paths (cheaper fallback models, cross-region failover) are currently coupled into the policy engine. We can create an exception toggle to treat fallback as a hard fail — requests that would have fallen back will return 503 with a short guidance payload.

Risks & mitigations:
1) Cache warmup: the quantized secure variant has a cold-start penalty; recommend a pre-warm step and an autoscale cushion for the first 24 hours.
2) Quality regressions: quantization may increase hallucinations on edge prompts; require a small eval set from CareBridge to validate quality before >10% traffic.
3) Operational impact: no-fallback increases apparent error rate; implement conservative autoscaling (buffer + SLA boundary) and a short-circuit abort (API: POST /ops/pilot-abort with reason).

Rollout proposal: 1% (metric gating for 24h) -> 10% (48h) -> 50% (72h) -> 100% (subject to exec sign-off). Gates: latency P95 < 400ms, error-rate < 0.5%, quality pass on eval set. Abort policy: immediate rollback if any gate fails.

I'll open INF-8241 with implementation tasks (routing toggle + control-plane UI flag + telemetry lines). ETA for implementation in staging: 4 business days.

- Rishi Malhotra
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime

- Enforced model pin to redwood-secure-1b-quant (no automated variant substitution).
- No-fallback policy enabled for the pilot; requests that would fall back will return a 503 and an incident will auto-create for ops triage.

Gating checklist (must be complete before we move beyond 10% traffic):

2) CareBridge provides a 200-300 example eval set for quality validation.
3) Pre-flight load test with agreed throughput targets.
4) Access to the S3 audit path for logs; retention set to 180 days for the pilot.
